issue_context.title: Memory usage of apiserver still spikes caused by many watcher terminated after using suggestedWatchChannelSize
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We have a relative large cluster with >800 nodes, and some daemonset watching >8000 CR instances running on every node. These CRs are upated very frequently. 

After applying suggestedWatchChannelSize improvements on watcher channel size, we still got apiserver memort usage spikes repeatedly, even oom, caused by too many watcher terminated due to small channel size and unresponsiveness and then too many relist all CR instances. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/63291172/227457763-38b595c3-1673-4d20-b1a0-ce7aad71b5a1.png)


### What did you expect to happen?

Set big enough channel size for watchers to avoid watcher terminated too many times. Actually before the PR of #109708, we hardcoded the channel size of that CRD to 1000 to fix this issue, and the memory usage is very smooth.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/63291172/227460269-82312c63-dfcc-41e6-acf7-1c74daadfc89.png)

- [ ] 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This issue occurred in our production cluster. To mimic the behaviour, at least observe the terminated_watchers metrics, we can
1. launch local cluser
2. create some CRD, i.e. mycrds and 5000 instances of mycrds
3. start 50 updater to keep updating these instances 
4. start 300 watchers to watch mycrds
5. observe `apiserver_terminated_watchers_total` for mycrds and kube-apiserver memory usage.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

review_comments:
I'm against doing this.

The pattern that you described in the parent bug (watching frequently changing resources from every node) is an anti-pattern of doing things. By allowing larger buffers we effectively increase memory usage of apiserver and I don't want to do that without a better reason.
Would it be beneficial to include a flag for users to adjust settings here?
That I would be fine with.

In large clusters (say 5k nodes), with 150k pods, given that each pod by default is mounting its default service account, by default we have 150,000 watches.

So we will effectively end-up with having chanSize of 1000 (it will be descrease to maxSize below) for each of those watches. And that is a huge waste of resources.

We can't do this - you need to come with something else.

instead of changing this all-over-the-place, I would prefer to pass some callback like `onUnresponsiveReceiver` during cacheWatcher creation.
It should be much simpler to plug this in.

/cc @wojtek-t
The TODO item here may be addressed by this change.

This is very problematic.
This can be caused by slow client (e.g. we have a slow client that just doesn't read events and is periodically shutdown). If apiserver is running for long enough, terminatedWatchCount will grow to a large value and pretty much every watch will have a large channel.
This change isn't safe to do.
